mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicates persistent inflation, which typically leads to higher real interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% and remains above that level for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that dampens corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% and an increase in industrial production above 115.0 (index) signals an overheating economy, which typically triggers a central bank tightening and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5 and INDPRO > 115.0, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for 3 consecutive months), a rising CPIAUCSL (indicating persistent inflation) leads to further rate hikes and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 (index) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 110.0, or the Rank IC over 2 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1800.0 (thousands of units) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1800.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% and a rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200.0 (thousands) signals an exceptionally tight labor market that accelerates wage inflation and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS > 200.0, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.
